title: Cohort-randomized trials for adaptive microbatch + KV prewarm policies (metrics, dashboards, rollback)
creator: Ava Martin
description: Run a controlled, cohort-randomized experiment to evaluate combined adaptive microbatching and KV-prefetch (prewarm) policies on production traffic segments. The goal is to quantify token-cost savings and end-to-end latency/SLAs with statistically sound analysis while providing a clear, automatable rollback path if quality or reliability regressions appear. This ticket covers experiment design, telemetry queries, dashboard spec, statistical plan, rollout cadence, and an operational rollback playbook.
hypothesis: Applying an adaptive microbatch policy with proactive KV prewarm for repeat sessions will reduce per-token GPU cost by >=10% for high-reuse cohorts without increasing 95th-percentile tail latency by more than 10% or increasing user-visible error rates.
primary_metrics: unit_cost_per_token (USD) — token billing and infra cost attribution normalized per model-inference token
user_visible_error_rate — percentage of responses with model error or gateway error
secondary_metrics: throughput_rps — requests per second per node
kv_prefetch_hit_ratio — fraction of requests served with warmed KV cache
avg_generation_tokens — average generated tokens per request
cpu_gpu_utilization — infra utilization to validate no overcommit
instrumentation: Prometheus metric names and tags to use: redwood_inference_token_cost_total{model,team,cohort}, redwood_inference_latency_seconds_bucket{le,model,cohort}, redwood_inference_errors_total{type,model,cohort}, redwood_inference_kv_prefetch_hits_total{cohort}, redwood_inference_requests_total{cohort}. Example PromQL for p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_latency_seconds_bucket{cohort=~".*"}[5m])) by (le,cohort)). Unit cost query (approx): sum(rate(redwood_inference_token_cost_total{cohort=~".*"}[1h])) / sum(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total{cohort=~".*"}[1h])). Instrumentation tasks: tag all requests with cohort id at the routing layer, ensure KV-prefetch metrics emitted per request, and add a tracer span for prewarm and batch_deliver stages.
sample_size_and_stats: Planned test: two-arm randomized cohort split, A: control (current policy), B: treatment (adaptive microbatch + prewarm). For cost reduction (continuous metric), use bootstrap CIs and a difference-in-means estimate with 95% CI. For tail latency, use non-parametric Mann-Whitney U and compute p95 distribution via bootstrapped samples. Preliminary sample size calc: to detect 10% cost reduction with sigma estimated at 0.25 * mean, alpha=0.05, power=0.8, required N per arm ~ 25,000 requests across target cohort. Use sequential analysis with a max duration of 7 days and pre-specified stopping rules. Document randomization seed and never change assignment mid-run for a given cohort member.
assignment_method: Cohort assignment via hashed client_id: cohort = hash(client_id, secret_salt) mod 100. Target cohorts: select two traffic cohorts with high session reuse: replication-cohort-31 and replication-cohort-44. Only users mapped into the selected cohort_ids are eligible. Avoid sticky routing changes; keep consistent mapping during experiment.
ramp_and_schedule: Rollout plan: day 0: dry-run on synthetic traffic (internal) for 2 hours. Day 1: 0.5% of selected cohort traffic for 4 hours. Day 2: 2% for 12 hours. Day 3: 10% for 24 hours. Day 4: 50% for 24 hours. Day 5: 100% for 48 hours. At each step, run analysis notebook and verify no trigger conditions. Each ramp step requires a brief sign-off from oncall and PM. Max experiment window 14 days if traffic volume low.
dashboard_spec: Grafana dashboard spec (high-level): Panel 1: Primary unit cost time series by cohort (1h downsample) with band showing 95% CI. Panel 2: Latency histograms and p95 time series by cohort. Panel 3: Error rate time series and error breakdown by type. Panel 4: KV prefetch hit ratio and prewarm CPU/GPU overhead. Panel 5: Traffic distribution and assignment sanity. Panel 6: Automated experiment health indicator - green/yellow/red computed from threshold rules. Dashboard link (placeholder): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/experiments/batching-prefetch-cohort-61299. Create derived panels that show relative change (treatment / control - 1) with annotated ramp events.
rollback_triggers: absolute p95 latency increase > 15% sustained over 30 minutes
user_visible_error_rate increase > 0.5 percentage points compared to control sustained for 15 minutes
infrastructure saturation: GPU utilization > 92% for > 10 minutes
unexpected model correctness regression detected by eval harness (quality_score drop > 3 points)
rollback_playbook: 1) Automatic: deployment controller watches experiment health metric. If a trigger fires, force-set cohort assignment to control for affected cohort and mark experiment paused. 2) Ops: Pager to inference-oncall. Immediate steps: (a) set policy to control via feature-flag toggle, (b) scale up capacity if needed to relieve tail, (c) collect debug traces and sample request IDs for repro. 3) Post-incident: run the postmortem template, tag the run as 'rolled_back', and schedule a follow-up with PM/Research to determine root cause before any re-run. 4) Communication: update #inference-experiments Slack channel and create an incident summary doc in Confluence. 5) Re-introduction gated by fixes and a new dry-run from start.
acceptance_criteria: Observed unit_cost_per_token reduction >= 10% with 95% CI excluding 0
No meaningful increase to p95 latency (>10%) or user_visible_error_rate
No infra saturation or increased operational toil during the ramp
All telemetry and dashboards populated and validated
analysis_artifacts_and_queries: Notebook: gs://redwood-infra/experiments/eng-61299/analysis.ipynb (draft). Example SQL to compute cost per token per cohort: SELECT cohort, SUM(token_cost_usd)/SUM(tokens_generated) as unit_cost FROM inference_billing_hourly WHERE experiment_run='ENG-61299' GROUP BY cohort; Example PromQL to compute error rate: sum(rate(redwood_inference_errors_total{experiment='ENG-61299'}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total{experiment='ENG-61299'}[5m])). Store raw sampled traces in s3://redwood-traces/eng-61299/.
notes: This experiment prioritizes operational safety over aggressive cost savings. If small improvements are observed in narrow cohorts, plan for a follow-up experiment that tests cross-cohort generalization and quantizes policies for cheap models. Coordinate with the Console team to expose recommended settings in Optimize recommendations if the treatment is validated. Make sure product and research own quality evaluation guards before large-scale rollouts.
next_steps: 1) Finalize instrumentation PR and merge by 2025-03-12. 2) Build Grafana dashboard and alert rules by 2025-03-14. 3) Run synthetic dry-run and validate queries by 2025-03-17. 4) Start cohort rollouts per ramp plan beginning 2025-03-18. 5) Post-run analysis and decision by 2025-04-01.
